Demo 4b: the PLL holding lock, models and RTL only

Locked: the divided clock runs at 10.001704 MHz against 10.001401 MHz asked for (+0.0030%, tolerance 2%), and the control voltage moved 0.192 mV across the measured window. Generated models around the design's own RTL: no transistors in this run.

oscillator rate, each cycle (thin) the same, averaged over each reference cycle (thick) up pulse (drawn as +1) down pulse (drawn as -1) reference clock (thick) oscillator divided by 40 (thin)
unpacking the waveforms...

Drag across the plot to zoom into that stretch. Scroll to zoom around the pointer, Shift+scroll (or the arrow keys) to slide along the run, double-click to see the whole run again. Hover to read every trace at one instant.

What this is: demo 4b's whole phase-locked loop. The charge pump, loop filter and ring oscillator are the models spice2rnm generated from the transistor netlist; the phase detector and the divide-by-40 are the design's own RTL, unchanged. One simulator, xezim, runs all of it. Nothing here is a transistor.

How it was recorded: the generated loop file was run again in a scratch copy with one change, four lines asking xezim to record its nets. That run printed exactly the lines the demo's own run printed, and this page was refused if it had not. The window shaded in the plots is the one the run measured in: it opened at 20.00 us and closed at 25.00 us, as the file declares.

Reading it, top to bottom. The control voltage is the loop's memory: the charge pump nudges it up or down once per reference cycle and it holds its value in between. This oscillator runs SLOWER as the control voltage rises (measured: its rate falls from 804.5 MHz to 16.74 MHz across 0.495 to 2.805 V), so the loop settles where the rate is 40 times the reference.

The oscillator panel is worked out from the recording: one value per cycle, 1 / (time between two rising crossings of 1.65 V, the threshold the loop's clock is taken at).

This run HOLDS lock rather than finding it. The netlist's initial condition starts the control voltage at 1.849 V, already beside where the loop settles, so the oscillator's first cycle is at 402.2 MHz and it is within 2% of 400.056 MHz from 3.75 ns to the end. What the page shows is the loop keeping the oscillator there, cycle after cycle, not pulling it in from far away.

The thin trace wobbles because the oscillator does: its period varies by 11.31 ps rms from one cycle to the next (0.45% of its 2499.6 ps period, over 9599 cycles). The netlist puts noise on the supply (vdd on node dd: trnoise, 20 mV rms, a new value every 100 ps), the generated loop drives that same noisy supply, and a ring oscillator's speed follows its supply. spice2rnm measured 11.98 ps rms on the transistor oscillator under that noise (at 1.85 V on its control, over 200 cycles, about 5% uncertain), so the model carries the circuit's jitter, not an artefact of the plot. The thick trace averages each reference cycle's 40 oscillator cycles, which is what the loop steers: after the first microsecond it stays between 398.957 and 401.091 MHz, against 400.056 MHz asked for.

Inside the measured window the control voltage stays between 1.8485 and 1.8505 V (it ends the run at 1.8497 V). The up and down pulses there average 347 ps and 471 ps wide: at lock the detector still fires on every reference edge, briefly, and the charges the two pulses push nearly cancel, which is why the control voltage drifts by only 0.192 mV over the window's 49 reference cycles.

Scope: this is one start from the initial condition the netlist states, at one reference rate and one corner. It shows that the models and the RTL lock together; it is not evidence about the transistors, which demo 4a compares against at the cost of a co-simulation.

Every point the recorded run wrote is in this page (times to 1 fs, voltages to 0.1 µV), except the oscillator rate, which is worked out from it. Each net is drawn the way the simulator holds it: a value stays until the next change, then steps. It loads nothing from the network. Built by harness/pll_wave.py in the spice2rnm demos.
